name: Automate marketplace and gateway settlement-to-ledger posting
what: Unbundle every marketplace and gateway payout (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, Amazon settlements) into commission, fixed fee, shipping fee, marketplace-facilitator sales tax withheld, 1099-K reportable totals and refunds, and post one journal entry per settlement instead of one lump-sum bank deposit.
encompasses: Match every settlement report to the order-level sales register
Split commission, fixed fee, collection fee, shipping fee and ad-spend deductions into separate ledger accounts
Book marketplace-facilitator sales tax withheld and 1099-K gross totals as separate line items
India only: book Section 52 TCS and GST on marketplace fees as separate line items (reads null for US brands)
Flag unexplained variance between expected fee and charged fee per order
Book revenue to the sale date, not the T+5 or T+7 payout date
Trace return and failed-delivery/return-to-sender deductions back to the original order
Produce one import-ready file per marketplace or gateway
outputs: Variance report by order and fee type
trigger: Each settlement cycle, or on founder request
founder_sees: The variance report and the draft journal entries before they post to the ledger

name: Reconcile payout deposits daily (gateway, marketplace, and COD where it applies)
what: Track what every payout source (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, Amazon and other marketplace settlements) says it paid against what actually lands in the bank, age the gap by source, and escalate deposits stuck past the source's own payout schedule. For an India-selling brand that also runs COD, track cash collected by every courier against what has actually been remitted, the same way, as a market option.
encompasses: Pull payout/deposit status per order per source: Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, Amazon settlements and other marketplaces
Compute days-outstanding since the expected payout date for every undeposited amount
Compare against each source's stated payout schedule (e.g. T+2 rolling, marketplace bi-weekly)
Flag sources whose undeposited balance is rising, not falling
Separate chargeback/dispute reversals and refund holds from genuine payout deductions
Roll the outstanding payout balance into the cash forecast as a receivable

India only: pull COD collection and remittance status per order per courier, compute days-outstanding since delivery, compare against each courier's stated remittance SLA (T+2 to T+8), and separate RTO cash reversals from genuine delivered-COD remittance (reads null for US brands)
inputs: Gateway and marketplace payout/settlement exports (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, Amazon)
India only: courier aggregator API or portal exports
outputs: Daily payout reconciliation and aging report by source
List of orders past SLA with amount at risk
trigger: Daily
tools: gateway/marketplace payout APIs (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal, Amazon Seller Central)
courier aggregator API (ClickPost/Shipway class, India COD only)
founder_sees: The aging report and which payout sources (or, for India COD, which couriers) are past SLA on remittance

name: Run chargeback and dispute representment
what: Own the chargeback and dispute lifecycle end to end: track reason codes, assemble the evidence packet the network or PayPal requires, file representment before the deadline, and track win rate by reason code and gateway.
encompasses: Pull every chargeback and dispute from each gateway/processor (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal) with its reason code and deadline
Assemble the evidence packet per reason code: proof of delivery, customer communication, IP/device match, policy acceptance
File representment before the network or PayPal deadline, never late
Track representment win rate by reason code, gateway and product
Escalate a rising chargeback rate against the processor's own threshold before the account gets flagged
Feed confirmed friendly-fraud patterns back to the fraud-control capability (MONEY-C42)
inputs: Gateway/processor dispute feed (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal)
brand brain: return and refund policy text
outputs: Chargeback win-rate report by reason code and gateway
trigger: As disputes arrive, weekly rollup
tools: gateway dispute APIs (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal)
founder_sees: Disputes needing a human call, and the win-rate trend by reason code

name: Automate accounts payable capture, matching and approval routing
what: Capture every vendor bill, match it to a purchase order and receipt, route it through an approval chain by amount and vendor, and schedule payment on the agreed terms.
encompasses: Extract vendor, amount, line items and due date from an incoming bill (email or upload)
Three-way match the bill to a purchase order and a goods-receipt or delivery confirmation
Route for approval by amount threshold and cost center, with automatic escalation if unreviewed
Flag duplicate bills and bills outside the agreed price or quantity
Schedule payment to land on the agreed due date, not early or late
Maintain a payables aging list by vendor
trigger: On bill receipt, and weekly for the aging review
founder_sees: Bills awaiting approval, any duplicate or price-mismatch flag, and the payment schedule

name: Manage accounts receivable and B2B or wholesale collections
what: Invoice wholesale and B2B buyers on their agreed terms, track every invoice to collection, and run a structured dunning sequence on anything overdue.
encompasses: Generate and send invoices on Net-30/Net-60 terms with the correct sales-tax and resale-certificate treatment (GST treatment for India-selling brands)
Track invoice status: open, partially paid, overdue, disputed
Age receivables by customer and by days overdue
Send a scheduled dunning sequence (reminder, follow-up, final notice) before escalation
Flag customers approaching or over their credit limit before the next order ships
Reconcile partial payments and credit notes against the right invoice
trigger: On invoice due date, and weekly for aging review
founder_sees: The aging report and the drafted dunning emails before they are sent

name: Run payroll processing and state statutory filings
what: Process payroll each cycle through Gusto or ADP and prepare the filings that go with it: federal and state withholding, state new-hire and unemployment-insurance registration per state an employee works in, W-2 at year end for employees, and 1099-NEC for contractors. India-selling brands with local staff run the equivalent PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS and Form 16 cycle as a market option; that path reads null for US-only brands.
encompasses: Compute gross-to-net pay from salary/hourly structure, timesheets and PTO data
Calculate federal and state income-tax withholding, FICA, and state unemployment insurance per employee's work state
Register the brand for payroll tax in every new state before the first paycheck there
Generate payslips (via Gusto or ADP) and the payroll register
Track final-pay rules by state for exits (some states require same-day or next-day final pay)
Generate W-2 for employees and 1099-NEC for contractors at year end, and file with the SSA/IRS

India only: calculate PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS deductions, prepare the PF ECR file, ESI return and TDS challan, and generate Form 16 and the annual TDS return at year end (reads null for US brands)
inputs: Payroll tax rate tables by state
India only: CTC structures, investment declarations, statutory rate tables (PF, ESI, PT, TDS slabs)
outputs: Draft state registration and withholding filings
India only: draft statutory filing files (PF/ESI/TDS), Form 16
trigger: Payroll cycle (weekly, biweekly or semimonthly), annually for W-2/1099-NEC (or Form 16 for India)

external_write.surface: Gusto or ADP, and state statutory portals

founder_sees: The payroll register and every statutory filing draft before submission

name: Maintain the fixed asset register and depreciation schedule
what: Keep one register of every asset the brand owns (equipment, fixtures, website build cost, packaging dies) with purchase date, useful life and a running depreciation schedule.
encompasses: Log every capital purchase above the capitalization threshold
Assign useful life and depreciation method per asset class
Compute monthly depreciation and post it to the P&L
Track disposals and write-offs
Reconcile the register to the balance sheet fixed-asset line each period
trigger: Monthly, and on every capital purchase
founder_sees: The updated register and the monthly depreciation entry

name: Manage employee expense and corporate card reconciliation
what: Collect receipts for every reimbursable expense and corporate card charge, apply the travel-and-expense policy, and reconcile the card statement to the ledger.
encompasses: Match card statement lines to submitted receipts
Flag charges with no receipt or outside policy (amount, category, vendor)
Apply the correct sales-tax treatment for reimbursable purchases where eligible (GST input-credit treatment for India-selling brands)
Route reimbursement requests for approval by amount
Reconcile the monthly card statement to the ledger with a named cause for any gap
Maintain the written travel-and-expense policy itself
trigger: Monthly card cycle
founder_sees: The reconciled statement and any out-of-policy or missing-receipt flags

name: Prepare the fundraising data room and lender or investor reporting pack
what: Assemble and keep current the data room a lender or investor asks for, and produce the recurring reporting pack (monthly update, covenant compliance, board deck financials) once financing is in place.
encompasses: Build the standard data room checklist (financials, cap table, contracts, IP, compliance filings)
Keep the cap table current with every round, grant and exercise
Draft the monthly investor or lender update from the metric contract and the P&L
Track loan covenants against the actual numbers and flag a breach before it happens
Prepare the financial slides for a board deck from the same source numbers as the dashboard
Redact anything a specific reader should not see
outputs: Data room folder structure and checklist
trigger: On a raise or loan process, monthly for reporting, quarterly for the board deck
founder_sees: The full data room checklist status and the drafted update before it goes to a lender or investor

name: Procure and track business insurance
what: Identify the insurance coverage an e-commerce brand needs (product liability, cyber, business owner's policy, D&O once there are outside investors), compare quotes, and track the renewal calendar and any claim.
encompasses: Map the brand's actual risk exposure (product category, data held, inventory value, outside investors) to coverage types
Compare quotes and coverage limits, not just premium
Track every policy's renewal date, limit and deductible in one calendar
Flag a coverage gap when the business changes (new product category, new country, new data type)
Log and track any claim from filing to settlement
trigger: Annually at renewal, and on a material business change
founder_sees: The coverage comparison and the renewal calendar with any flagged gap

name: Reconcile multi-currency and cross-border payments
what: For a brand selling or paying suppliers across currencies, convert every foreign-currency transaction at the right rate, reconcile the payment processor's settlement to the bank, and flag FX gain or loss separately from operating margin.
encompasses: Pull the daily or transaction-date FX rate used by the payment processor
Reconcile Payoneer, Wise or PayPal settlement reports to the bank deposit
Separate realized FX gain or loss from product margin in the P&L
Track outstanding foreign-currency payables to suppliers
Flag a rate move large enough to change a landed-cost assumption
trigger: Each settlement cycle
founder_sees: The FX gain/loss report and any rate move large enough to matter

name: Build and maintain the brand's data warehouse and ETL pipeline
what: Land Shopify, Meta, GA4, the ESP, marketplaces and the payment processor into one warehouse on a schedule, so every dashboard and report reads from the same tables instead of five separate exports.
encompasses: Define the schema for orders, sessions, ad spend, email/SMS sends and marketplace settlements
Build the scheduled sync from each source into the warehouse
Handle schema drift when a source changes its export format
Deduplicate and backfill on a failed or late sync
Expose one governed semantic layer so a metric means the same thing everywhere
Alert when a source has not synced within its expected window
inputs: Shopify, Meta, GA4, ESP, marketplace and payment processor exports or APIs
trigger: Scheduled (daily or hourly per source), and on schema-change alert
founder_sees: The sync freshness log and any source that has gone stale

name: Run a governed ask-the-data analyst over the brand's own metric contract
what: Let the founder or a specialist ask a plain-language question and get back a number computed from the metric contract, with its definition, freshness stamp and source, instead of an ungoverned guess.
encompasses: Parse the question into the metric-contract terms it maps to
Compute the answer in code from the warehouse, never from model arithmetic
State the exact window, definition and freshness stamp used
Say plainly when the data needed is missing or stale instead of estimating
Log every question asked, for a FAQ of what the founder actually wants to know
Refuse a question that needs a metric the contract does not define, and say what would need to be added
outputs: Answer with number, definition, window and freshness stamp
trigger: On demand (chat, SMS or dashboard query; WhatsApp where the brand uses it, market option for IN/EU/LATAM)
founder_sees: The answer plus the definition and freshness stamp it was computed with

name: Build marketing mix modeling for cross-channel budget allocation
what: Model total revenue against spend across every channel (including channels that cannot be pixel-tracked, like offline, brand search and word of mouth) to size each channel's real contribution and suggest a budget split.
encompasses: Assemble weekly spend by channel alongside total revenue and baseline (organic/direct) revenue
Fit a model that separates each channel's marginal contribution from the baseline
Account for adstock and diminishing returns per channel
Cross-check the model's implied CAC against the platform-reported CAC and flag the gap
Simulate a reallocated budget split and its expected revenue effect
Refresh the model on a fixed cadence, never mid-campaign
trigger: Monthly or quarterly refresh
founder_sees: The channel contribution estimates and the gap against platform-reported CAC

name: Build RFM and cohort segmentation models for the customer base
what: Score every customer on recency, frequency and monetary value, group them into named segments, and track how many customers move between segments each period.
encompasses: Compute recency, frequency and monetary value per customer from order history
Assign each customer to a named segment (e.g. champion, at-risk, lapsed, new)
Track segment migration month over month
Size the revenue and customer count in each segment
Flag a segment whose size or value is moving against the brand's history
Hand segment membership to the Lifecycle specialist for targeting, without duplicating the scoring logic there
trigger: Weekly or monthly refresh
founder_sees: The segment sizes, their trend, and any segment moving against history

name: Audit and configure tag management and server-side tracking
what: Audit the tag management layer itself (not just GA4 or the Meta pixel individually): container structure, server-side tagging, consent mode gating, and duplicate or dead tags firing on the site.
encompasses: Inventory every tag firing on the site and who owns it
Check container structure and versioning discipline (staging vs live)
Assess whether server-side tagging would fix data loss from browser blocking
Verify consent mode gates tags correctly by region
Find duplicate, conflicting or dead tags still firing
Document the tag map so a new tag never gets added blind
outputs: Server-side tagging recommendation with expected data-quality gain
trigger: Quarterly, or after any major site or app change
founder_sees: The tag inventory and every duplicate, dead or misconfigured tag

name: Manage freelancer and contractor engagements
what: Run the full lifecycle of a freelance or contractor engagement: scope of work, IP assignment, rate agreement, invoicing against milestones, and renewal or offboarding at the end.
encompasses: Draft a scope of work with deliverables, rate and IP assignment clause
Track milestone completion against the agreed scope before approving an invoice
Maintain one roster of active freelancers with rate, category and renewal date
Flag a freelancer doing recurring work that should convert to a role or a retainer
Route contractor invoices through the same approval chain as vendor bills
Run a short offboarding step (access revocation, final invoice, IP handover) at engagement end
trigger: On engagement start, at each milestone, and at engagement end
founder_sees: The roster, any engagement that should convert to a role, and invoices awaiting milestone approval

name: Draft and review vendor and employment legal contracts
what: Keep a standard set of contract templates (NDA, MSA, vendor agreement, employment agreement) and run every incoming contract through a redline checklist before the founder signs.
encompasses: Maintain current templates for NDA, MSA, vendor agreement and employment agreement
Redline an incoming vendor or partner contract against a standard checklist (liability cap, termination notice, data handling, exclusivity)
Flag any clause outside the brand's standard terms in plain language
Track contract expiry and auto-renewal dates in one calendar
Maintain a signed-contract repository with the current version of each
Never advise on a jurisdiction-specific legal question without naming that limit
trigger: On every new or renewing contract
founder_sees: Every flagged clause and the contract calendar before anything is signed

name: Maintain the employee handbook and HR policies
what: Keep one current handbook covering leave, work-from-home, code of conduct and state-specific requirements like mandatory anti-harassment training (California, New York, Illinois and others), and confirm every employee has acknowledged the current version.
encompasses: Draft and update leave, WFH, expense and code-of-conduct policies as the team grows
Maintain state-mandated anti-harassment training and policy where required (e.g. California SB 1343, New York, Illinois, Connecticut)
India only: maintain the POSH (workplace harassment) policy and committee as legally required in India (reads null for US brands)
Track which employees have acknowledged the current handbook version
Flag a policy that is silent on a situation that just came up
Version the handbook so an old copy is never the one in circulation
trigger: On hire growth milestones, or annually
founder_sees: The current handbook version and the acknowledgement gap list

name: Run structured employee offboarding
what: Run one checklist for every exit: same-day access revocation, asset return, knowledge transfer, exit interview and final settlement, so nothing is left half-done after someone leaves.
encompasses: Trigger same-day revocation of every system the person had access to
Recover company assets (laptop, phone, keys) and confirm return
Run a knowledge-transfer checklist for anything only that person knew
Conduct or prepare a structured exit interview
Compute the full-and-final settlement (pending leave, bonus, dues) correctly
Confirm every step closed before marking the offboarding complete
trigger: On resignation or termination notice
founder_sees: The checklist completion status, especially access revocation and the settlement number

name: Monitor 3PL and warehouse SLA performance daily
what: Track the day-to-day performance of every 3PL and warehouse against its written SLA: pick-and-pack speed, mis-ship rate, damage rate and backorder rate, and flag a breach before it becomes a pattern.
encompasses: Pull daily fulfillment timestamps (order to pack to ship) per warehouse
Compute mis-ship, damage and backorder rate against the SLA target
Flag a single-day spike separately from a trend that is drifting
Tie a fulfillment delay to its downstream effect (late delivery, failed-delivery/return-to-sender risk, review risk; RTO risk where the brand runs India COD, market option)
Feed confirmed SLA misses into the vendor's quarterly review with a dated log
outputs: Breach log with dates and cause
trigger: Daily
founder_sees: The daily scorecard and any SLA breach with its likely cause

name: Build and maintain the CS knowledge base, macros and QA scoring
what: Keep the customer-service knowledge base and canned-response macros current with the brand's actual policies, and score a sample of tickets each week against a written quality rubric.
encompasses: Write and update macros from the brand's current policy (shipping, returns, warranty) whenever a policy changes
Flag a macro that contradicts the current policy or a claim tier
Score a sample of resolved tickets each week against a written quality rubric
Track first-response time, resolution time and reopen rate by macro category
Surface the most common ticket reasons back to the specialist who owns that root cause
trigger: Weekly, and whenever a policy changes
founder_sees: The QA score sample and any macro flagged as out of date

name: Audit and enforce email authentication for sending domains
what: Check SPF, DKIM, DMARC and BIMI on every domain the brand sends email from (transactional, marketing, support) and move the DMARC policy from monitor-only to enforced without breaking deliverability.
encompasses: Inventory every domain and subdomain used to send email
Check SPF record validity and the 10-lookup limit
Verify DKIM selectors are configured and rotating
Check the current DMARC policy (none, quarantine, reject) and its reporting address
Read DMARC aggregate reports to find unauthorized senders before tightening the policy
Step the policy from none to quarantine to reject only once reports show no legitimate mail failing
inputs: DNS records for every sending domain
trigger: Quarterly, or before any bulk-sender requirement change
founder_sees: The authentication status per domain and the staged plan to reach reject

name: Inventory and rotate API keys, tokens and service credentials
what: Keep one inventory of every API key, token and service credential the brand's tools use, who or what holds it, when it was last rotated, and rotate on a schedule or after any staff exit.
encompasses: Inventory every API key and token across connected tools (payment gateway, ESP, ad platforms, warehouse)
Record scope, owner and last-rotation date for each
Flag a credential with excess scope (more access than the integration needs)
Rotate on a fixed schedule and immediately after any relevant staff exit
Move credentials out of code, spreadsheets or chat into a secrets manager
Confirm an old credential is actually revoked, not just replaced
inputs: List of connected tools and integrations
outputs: Credential inventory with scope and rotation date
trigger: Quarterly, and immediately on staff exit

external_write.surface: secrets manager and each connected tool

founder_sees: The credential inventory and any over-scoped or overdue-for-rotation key

name: Confirm PCI DSS scope and complete the merchant self-assessment questionnaire
what: Determine which PCI DSS self-assessment questionnaire applies given how the brand takes payment, confirm the checkout does not touch raw card data outside that scope, and complete the SAQ on schedule.
encompasses: Determine SAQ type from the checkout's payment flow (hosted fields, redirect, or direct card capture)
Confirm no raw card data is logged, emailed or stored outside the payment processor's scope
Walk the applicable SAQ checklist and collect evidence for each control
Flag any control the brand cannot currently attest to
Track the compliance attestation date and the next renewal
trigger: Annually, or on any checkout payment-flow change
founder_sees: The SAQ type, any unmet control, and the attestation renewal date
human_role: IT/security or payment processor's compliance team

name: Run staff security awareness training and phishing simulation
what: Run a recurring phishing simulation and short security training for every staff member with admin access, and track who clicks, who reports, and who needs a repeat.
encompasses: Send a simulated phishing email on a recurring schedule
Track click rate, report rate and repeat-offender pattern
Assign a short follow-up training to anyone who clicked
Cover password hygiene, 2FA and how to report a suspicious message in the training
Report the trend (click rate improving or not) to the founder each quarter
trigger: Quarterly
founder_sees: The click-rate trend and who still needs a repeat training

name: Detect return and refund policy abuse
what: Find the customers and patterns that cost the brand through the return and refund process itself: wardrobing, serial high-return-rate customers, and refunds issued without a matching return.
encompasses: Compute return rate and refund-without-return rate per customer over time
Flag a customer whose return rate is far above the brand's own baseline
Detect wardrobing signals (worn/used item returned, tags removed) from support notes or photos
Cross-check refunds issued against actual received returns in the warehouse system
Recommend a policy response (flag for review, require prepayment or card-on-file, deny future return; restrict COD for India brands, market option) for the founder to approve
inputs: Order, return and refund history per customer
outputs: List of refunds with no matching return
trigger: Weekly
founder_sees: The risk-scored customer list and any refund with no matching return

name: Run vendor security and data-processing risk assessments
what: Before a new SaaS tool, ESP, 3PL or agency gets access to customer or payment data, run a standard risk questionnaire and confirm a data-processing agreement is signed.
encompasses: Send a standard security questionnaire to a new vendor before onboarding
Confirm the vendor's certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001) actually cover the service being used, not just the company
Confirm a data-processing agreement is signed before any customer data is shared
Classify each vendor by data sensitivity (none, PII, payment data)
Maintain one register of every vendor with data access, its risk tier and its DPA status
Re-assess a vendor on renewal or after a public breach disclosure
inputs: Data types the integration will access
trigger: Before onboarding, and on renewal or breach disclosure
founder_sees: The risk register and any vendor with data access but no signed DPA

name: Auto-draft SaaS renewal renegotiation before auto-renew windows close
what: Watch every SaaS contract's auto-renew date and usage data, and draft a renegotiation or cancellation email with the brand's own usage numbers before the window closes, instead of waiting for a tooling audit to catch it after the charge lands.
encompasses: Track every SaaS contract's renewal date and notice-period deadline in one calendar
Pull actual seat usage or API usage for that tool from the brand's own logs
Draft a renegotiation email citing the brand's usage against the current plan tier
Draft a cancellation email with the required notice period if usage does not justify the cost
Hand both drafts to the founder before the notice-period deadline, not after
inputs: SaaS contract terms and renewal dates
outputs: Drafted renegotiation or cancellation email per contract
trigger: On approaching notice-period deadline
founder_sees: The renewal calendar and the drafted email before the deadline

name: Auto-escalate aged payout remittance with SLA citations
what: Beyond just showing a dashboard of undeposited payout cash (gateway, marketplace or, for India COD, courier), draft the actual escalation email to the source's support or ops contact once a remittance passes its own written SLA, citing the specific order IDs and the SLA clause.
encompasses: Detect the exact day a payout or remittance crosses its source's own SLA (gateway, marketplace, or courier for India COD)
Pull the specific order IDs and amounts still outstanding for that source
Draft an escalation email citing the source's own SLA clause and the aged order list
Track whether the source responds and whether the cash actually lands after escalation
Roll a source's repeated SLA misses into its quarterly vendor review automatically
inputs: Payout/remittance status feed (gateway, marketplace, or courier for India COD)
Written SLA per contract or platform terms
trigger: On SLA breach
founder_sees: The escalation draft and whether the prior escalation actually recovered the cash

name: Simulate financing structures live against the rolling cash forecast
what: Instead of a one-time comparison of financing options, let the founder ask what a specific loan or revenue-based-financing structure would do to the 13-week cash forecast right now, and get a sensitivity table back in the same session.
encompasses: Take a proposed financing structure (amount, rate, repayment schedule) as an input
Re-run the existing rolling cash forecast with that structure layered in
Show the lowest cash point with and without the structure, side by side
Stress-test the structure against a slow-sales scenario, not just the base case
Flag a covenant or repayment date that would collide with a known low-cash week
outputs: Side-by-side cash forecast with and without the financing
trigger: On founder request
founder_sees: The side-by-side forecast and any covenant date colliding with a low-cash week

name: Correlate account-takeover signals across every connected system
what: No single tool today sees an anomaly that only shows up by comparing login geography and device across Shopify admin, the ad accounts, the ESP and the payment processor at once. Correlate them in one place and flag the pattern a single-tool audit would miss.
encompasses: Pull login timestamp, IP geography and device fingerprint from every admin-level system the brand uses
Flag a login to one system from a new geography shortly after a login to another system from a different geography
Flag a password-reset or new-device login on one system followed by a permission change on another
Correlate against the current staff travel or remote-work pattern before flagging, to cut false positives
Hand a confirmed pattern straight to the incident-response runbook, not just a dashboard
inputs: Login logs from every admin-level connected system
outputs: Cross-system anomaly flag with the correlated evidence
trigger: Continuous, reviewed daily
founder_sees: The correlated anomaly and the evidence from each system, before any action is taken

name: Plan Q4 holiday and promo-calendar cash peaks on top of the rolling forecast
what: Extend the rolling 13-week cash forecast to explicitly plan the peak-season cash squeeze: inventory pre-build financing before Q4 holiday (Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Prime Day) and other named-date peaks (Mother's Day, Father's Day, back to school, Valentine's Day, July 4), and sales-tax refund or credit timing that can free up cash. India-selling brands plan the same squeeze around Diwali and wedding season, with the COD collection lag and GST input-credit refund timing added as a market option that reads null for US-only brands.
encompasses: Layer the Q4/BFCM (or other named-peak) inventory pre-build cost onto the forecast weeks before the peak, not the week it ships
Track sales-tax refund or credit timing as a cash inflow, not just a compliance item
Flag the single lowest-cash week across the whole peak build-up, not just the current 13 weeks
Compare this year's peak cash plan to last year's actual peak cash low
India only: model the COD collection lag widening during Diwali/wedding-season peak (courier volume strain) and track GST input-credit refund timing (reads null for US brands)
outputs: Lowest-cash-week flag across the full peak build-up
trigger: Ahead of each major seasonal peak
founder_sees: The lowest cash point across the full peak build-up and what drives it

name: Prepare and file US state sales tax returns through Avalara or TaxJar
what: Beyond tracking where nexus exists, run the actual filing mechanics through Avalara or TaxJar: sync taxability and exemption/resale-certificate data, prepare and file the return in each registered state on its own schedule, and reconcile collected-vs-remitted before every filing. India-selling brands run the equivalent e-invoice, e-way bill and GSTR filing mechanics as a market option; that path reads null for US-only brands.
encompasses: Sync product taxability mappings and exemption/resale certificates into Avalara or TaxJar
Generate the return-ready transaction detail for every registered state each filing period
Prepare and file the state sales tax return on that state's own due date (monthly, quarterly or annual by state)
Reconcile sales tax collected against sales tax remitted per state before filing
Flag a mismatch between the ledger, the Avalara/TaxJar report and the state portal before the filing deadline

India only: generate a compliant e-invoice at point of sale, generate an e-way bill for shipments over the threshold, prepare GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, and reconcile input tax credit against GSTR-2B before filing (reads null for US brands)
inputs: Avalara or TaxJar taxability and filing status
India only: purchase register, GSTR-2B from the GST portal, e-invoice/e-way bill thresholds
outputs: India only: draft e-invoices, e-way bills, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, ITC mismatch report
trigger: Per each state's own filing schedule (India: per invoice/shipment for e-invoicing, monthly for GSTR-1/3B)

external_write.surface: Avalara or TaxJar, and state tax portals (India: GST portal / GSP connector)

tools: India only: GSP/e-invoice API or portal automation, ITC reconciliation script
founder_sees: The draft filings and any reconciliation mismatch before the deadline
human_role: e-commerce accountant / sales-tax practitioner (India: GST practitioner)

name: Source, screen and support offer negotiation, not just the hiring scorecard
what: Extend structured hiring past the scorecard and job ad into the actual sourcing and screening work: choosing outreach channels, running the first screen, and preparing the offer negotiation.
encompasses: Pick sourcing channels by role (LinkedIn, niche job boards, referral) instead of one default channel for every role
Draft outreach messages to passive candidates that reference the actual role artefact
Run a structured first-screen call script against the scorecard, not an open chat
Track candidate pipeline stage and time-in-stage per role
Prepare an offer with a band-consistent number and a negotiation range before the founder calls the candidate
trigger: Per open role
